t: #3572 Maximize Y-Sum by Picking a Triplet of Distinct X-Values
o: Pick three indices whose x-values are pairwise distinct, maximizing the sum of their y-values. Only the x-value identity matters, so for each distinct x we should always use its maximum y. Example 1: best y per x is {1:5, 2:3, 3:6} → 14. Example 2: only two distinct x-values → -1. With n up to 1e5 we need a linear/hash-based pass, not triple loops.
k: For each distinct x-value, only its maximum y can ever matter.
The answer is the sum of the three largest per-x maxima, or -1 if fewer than three distinct x-values exist.

a.n: Approach 1: Hash Map of Maxima + Top-3 Scan
a.i: Compress each x-group to its best y in one pass, then take the three largest compressed values. Any optimal triplet uses, for its three chosen x-values, the maximum y of each group, so this is exact.
s: If the map has fewer than 3 keys, return -1.
Sum the three largest values (sort the ≤ n distinct values, or track top 3 in one pass).
a.t: O(n log n) due to sorting the distinct values (O(n) if you track top-3 manually).

a.i: Same idea, but maintain the three largest per-x maxima in constant space while building the map, avoiding the sort entirely.
s: Iterate once, updating the per-x maximum.
Whenever a group's maximum updates (or a new group appears), feed the value into a running top-3 (a, b, c).
Return a+b+c if at least 3 distinct x-values were seen, else -1.
a.t: O(n) expected — one pass plus constant work per distinct value.
a.sp: O(n) for the hash map (the top-3 structure itself is O(1)).

w: Always reduce 'pick one per group' problems to per-group maxima first. Pitfall: forgetting the -1 case when fewer than three distinct x-values exist. Follow-up: generalize to picking p distinct values (top-p tracking or a size-p heap).
